semantic_changes.change: Numbers compare by calc_func's comparison rule, not by truncation to 15 significant digits: equal numbers are equal, two different numbers within a relative 1e-13 give an unknown verdict, and a call that verdict decides is refused (NotImplemented naming the range).
semantic_changes.reason: One comparison rule (honesty rule 5); Excel near-equality is owned by cdoc-jpha (the bead notes).

semantic_changes.change: Text compares by calc_func's text rule and patterns match ASCII text ignoring ASCII case; a pattern of * alone matches every text; beyond ASCII the verdict is unknown.
semantic_changes.reason: The bead notes: follow what calc_func's comparison does today and refuse where it refuses, rather than inventing a second collation (cdoc-jpha).

semantic_changes.change: A ~ resolves at parse: ~*, ~? and ~~ are the characters themselves, so a~*b matches the text a*b; a ~ before any other character, or at the end, is itself. The legacy kept the tilde in a criterion without an unescaped wildcard, so a~*b matched nothing.
semantic_changes.reason: The COUNTIF, SUMIF and COUNTIFS pages: a ~ before * or ? finds that character; the rest is unmeasured, and Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM read of probe cells on this machine (round 3) agrees: a~b meets the text a~b and not ab, a~ meets a~ and not a.

semantic_changes.change: A criterion operand is read by worksheet number coercion (plain decimal, at most 15 significant digits), and so is text in a range under = a number; text never meets <, <=, > or >= a number and always meets <> a number. Other text holding a digit is refused as a criterion and gives an unknown verdict as a range cell under = a number. The legacy read number text in the range under every operator.
semantic_changes.reason: Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads of a scratch copy of the oracle workbook on this machine (refuter 1 of round 1, and this round): number text meets a number criterion under = only, never under an ordering, and always under <>. Labels such as 2016-17 Winter are dc-e00t's; Excel's locale number-text rules are cfml-m2.6's.

semantic_changes.change: An empty cell given as the criterion is the number 0; the legacy matched blank cells.
semantic_changes.reason: The COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIF and MAXIFS pages: an empty criteria cell is treated as 0; the COUNTIF and SUMIF pages are silent, so their rows are unmeasured choices.

semantic_changes.change: "" matches blank cells and empty text, "=" blank cells only, "<>" every cell but a blank one; the legacy matched blank cells and empty text for both "" and "=".
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured choice; the oracle workbook holds the rows for a capture.

semantic_changes.change: <> with an operand holds wherever = does not: blank cells, and cells of another kind than the operand, meet it. The legacy failed every cell of another kind.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured choice; the oracle workbook holds the rows for a capture.

semantic_changes.change: Text naming an error literal (#NULL!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #REF!, #NAME?, #NUM!, #N/A) asks for cells holding that error under = and <>, and under <, <=, > and >= compares errors only, ordered as ERROR.TYPE numbers them; an error value given as the criterion asks for cells holding that error; the newer literals are refused. The legacy read the text as text and returned an error criterion as the result.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured choice; Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads on this machine (round 3) agree: COUNTIF over a #VALUE! cell with "#VALUE!" or #VALUE! is 1, COUNTIF(A1:A16,#N/A) and SUMIF(A1:A16,#N/A,B1:B16) count A12, and #DIV/0! meets <#N/A and <=#DIV/0! but not >=#N/A, <#DIV/0! or >#DIV/0!. The SUMIF page says only that matching the string #VALUE! gives incorrect results.

semantic_changes.change: A text cell spelling TRUE or FALSE under a logical criterion has an unknown verdict, and an ordering against a logical compares logicals, FALSE below TRUE; the legacy read such text as a logical and ordered logicals.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured; no page settles it. Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads (round 3) agree on the ordering: FALSE meets <TRUE, TRUE meets <=TRUE and >FALSE, and no cell of A1:A16 meets <TRUE or <FALSE.

semantic_changes.change: An omitted criterion is 0, as an empty cell given as the criterion is; the legacy returned #VALUE!.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured choice; Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads (round 3) agree: SUMIF(A1:A16,,B1:B16) = 16384, the row of the 0, and COUNTIF(A1:A16,) = COUNTIFS(A1:A16,) = 1.

semantic_changes.change: A range that is not a reference ends in ReferenceRequired; the legacy flattened arrays, and MAXIFS and MINIFS returned an array of #VALUE!.
semantic_changes.reason: Excel takes references there; lifting is cfml-m3.4.

semantic_changes.change: An argument count that does not form pairs is FunctionFault::ArityMismatch; the legacy returned #VALUE!.
semantic_changes.reason: Admission belongs to the call interface (cfunc-m1.1); the catalogue arity has no pair form, so the kernel reports it with the same fault.

semantic_changes.change: SUMIF's and AVERAGEIF's third argument is always taken from its top-left cell over the range's size, computed on GridArea, when that shaped range lies inside the reference the formula gives; one that extends past it, past the sheet's edge included, is refused. The legacy kept a third range of the same shape, otherwise re-resolved its A1 text, and returned #REF! past the edge.
semantic_changes.reason: The SUMIF and AVERAGEIF pages (top-left cell). The refusal keeps a stale value from being published as calculated on the engine route until dc-1mc8 makes the cells past the given reference the formula's prerequisites.

semantic_changes.change: The *IFS shapes are compared before any criterion or cell is read; the legacy read every range first.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured order; it also keeps a mismatched call from reading cells.

semantic_changes.change: Ranges are read sparsely through CellReader, one verdict per visited cell, and the blank rows of all ranges are counted at once; the legacy materialized every cell of every range.
semantic_changes.reason: The bead notes: a whole-column criteria range costs what the reader visits, as cfunc-m3.4 does.

semantic_changes.change: Sums and averages fold through Site::add and Site::divide, each an arithmetic site under the call's NumericMode (ExactUnavailable under Exact); an overflowing total is #NUM!, a zero is +0 and a subnormal result is refused. The legacy added f64 directly.
semantic_changes.reason: NumericMode reaches every arithmetic site (plan 5); the number rule of cfunc-m1.2.

semantic_changes.change: A criterion longer than 255 characters, operator and escapes included, is #VALUE!; a text cell longer than 255 characters has an unknown verdict under a text criterion or a pattern.
semantic_changes.reason: The COUNTIF and SUMIF pages say matching strings longer than 255 characters gives incorrect results; Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads (round 3) give #VALUE! for REPT("a",256), for "<>" joined to 254 or 255 characters, "=" or "<" joined to 255 and ">=" joined to 254, for REPT("a",255)&"*", for REPT("~*",128) and for a criterion cell holding 256 characters, and compute "<>" joined to 253 characters and REPT("a",255).

semantic_changes.change: A reference of several areas given as a range is refused.
semantic_changes.reason: Excel's result is not modelled; owned by dc-gdii (refuter 1's ad-hoc read of round 1: SUMIF((B3:B4,B6),"a") = #VALUE!).

semantic_changes.change: <, <=, > or >= with no operand meets no cell, as the legacy's blank operand did under an ordering; it is no longer refused.
semantic_changes.reason: Unmeasured choice; Excel 16.0's ad-hoc COM reads (round 3) give 0 for each of the four over A1:A16, which holds empty text and a blank cell.

Adding it on save and stripping it on load from catalogue metadata is dc-552j.
not_ported.basis: _xlfn (descriptions and notes: dc-552j)

items: an array given as a range (flattened by flatten_arg; MAXIFS and MINIFS returned an array of #VALUE! of its shape, extrema_ifs_direct_array_value_error), and an array or a reference of several cells given as a criterion, over which Excel lifts the function
not_ported.reason: A range is a reference: an array there ends in ReferenceRequired (at admission for a declared reference parameter, by the kernel for a criteria range past the declared ones); an array criterion and a criterion reference of several cells are refused as not modelled. Lifting a function over an array is array evaluation.
not_ported.basis: array lifting (notes: dc-ibp2 cites cfml-m3.4 for it); lift has no other hit that does the work (dc-8abf is the deferred scope epic, dc-ime9 is provenance, dc-1mc8 lifts a refusal of this bead); cfml-m3.4 (Preserve array evaluation and legacy array contexts) is the bead cfunc-m3.2 and cfunc-m3.4 name for array lifting

items: parse_excel_number: a criterion operand or a range cell read as a number by Rust f64 parsing of its trimmed text
not_ported.reason: Criterion operands, and range text under = a number, are read by worksheet number coercion (crates/calc-func/src/coerce.rs): the plain decimal form with at most 15 significant digits. Other text holding a digit is refused, because Excel may read it as a number: a label such as Q1 or 2016-17 Winter waits on the certain not-a-number verdict (dc-e00t), and a date, a fraction, a currency amount, grouped digits or a percentage on Excel's locale number-text rules (cfml-m2.6). A criterion built "op"&cell over a number also needs & to give the number's text (dc-q9rb).
not_ported.basis: NumberTextService and value-parsing (descriptions: cfml-m2.6), number-text and digit-bearing (descriptions: dc-e00t), number's text (descriptions: dc-q9rb).

items: compare_excel_numbers (excel_numeric_compare.rs): numbers compared after truncation to 15 significant digits, so 0.1+0.2 equals 0.3 under COUNTIF
not_ported.reason: calc_func has one comparison rule, the comparison operators' (crates/calc-func/src/catalogue/comparison.rs, numbers), which refuses two different numbers within a relative 1e-13; the criteria matcher calls it, so such a cell's verdict is unknown and a call it decides is refused. Excel's rule for nearly equal numbers comes from cdoc-jpha's capture.
not_ported.basis: nearly equal, near-equal (descriptions: cdoc-jpha; dc-r4ci owns the near-zero adjustment of + and -, not comparison; notes: cdoc-jpha, cfunc-m3.22, which routes the Exact refusal)

items: text equality, ordering and wildcard matching under Unicode to_lowercase (compare_texts in criteria_family.rs, wildcard_match in xmatch.rs)
not_ported.reason: Criteria text compares by the comparison operators' text rule (identical code units, or ASCII ignoring ASCII case; ordering on ASCII letters and digits only) and patterns match ASCII text ignoring ASCII case; anything beyond needs Excel's collation, so that cell's verdict is unknown and a call it decides is refused.
not_ported.basis: collation (descriptions: cdoc-jpha; notes: cfml-m1.3 and cfunc-m3.5 cite it)

functions_evidence: Per-ID manifest of the 8 IDs: what each implements, where its rule departs from Microsoft's page for it (divergent), and what it refuses (unsupported). '(documented)' marks a rule the page states and '(unmeasured)' one no page settles. No entry has been compared with Excel through calc_verdict: cfunc_m3_5__excel_comparison judges every row of the two cfunc_m3_5 cases in crates/calc-func/tests/fixtures/cfunc_m3_5/oracle.xlsx once `cargo xtask capture` writes crates/calc-func/tests/captures/cfunc_m3_5/oracle.capture.json, and is not_run with MissingCapture until then, so no parity is claimed. Excel 16.0 (build 20430) on this machine was read ad hoc by COM on a scratch copy of that workbook on 2026-10-21 (not a capture): every computed row of both cases agrees with that read (round 3: 117 computed rows, 0 differing), and the rows that cite it, or the probe cells read with it, say so. The documented rules are those of Microsoft's support pages, read on 2026-10-21: COUNTIF (e0de10c6-f885-4e71-abb4-1f464816df34), COUNTIFS (dda3dc6e-f74e-4aee-88bc-aa8c2a866842), SUMIF (169b8c99-c05c-4483-a712-1697a653039b), SUMIFS (c9e748f5-7ea7-455d-9406-611cebce642b), AVERAGEIF (faec8e2e-0dec-4308-af69-f5576d8ac642), AVERAGEIFS (48910c45-1fc0-4389-a028-f7c5c3001690), MAXIFS (dfd611e6-da2c-488a-919b-9b6376b28883) and MINIFS (6ca1ddaa-079b-4e74-80cc-72eef32e6599), each at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/<name>-function-<id>.
